newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Aid workers leave Goma after airport reopens.
newsitem.headline: Aid workers leave Goma after airport reopens.

text.p: Zairean government authorities reopened the airport at Goma on Sunday after a closure lasting several hours, allowing 18 foreign aid workers to fly out because of growing insecurity in eastern Zaire, an aid official said.
A U.N. spokesman in neighbouring Rwanda told Reuters that the Zairean authorities, after closing the airport without explanation, later withdrew the order and the aid workers left.
The abrupt closure order had left a group of aid workers stranded in the airport lounge. They had gone to Goma airport, the largest in eastern Zaire, to join a U.N. flight via Uganda to Kenya.
From Bukavu, at the southern end of Lake Kivu, a 27-seater plane evacuated French and Italian nationals, including diplomats, aid workers and civilians, without incident on Sunday.

Bukavu was tense as the sound of distant cannon fire from the south echoed round the town, and Zairean troops, recently reinforced, were noticeably nervous. Witnesses said there were no civilians on the streets, and many people were seen loading up cars and trucks ready to move out of the town.
On Saturday the United Nations sent two planes to Bukavu to evacuate 128 U.N. and other foreign workers after conflict between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops threatened to engulf the region.
World Food Programme spokeswoman Brenda Barton in Nairobi said there were still about 100 international aid workers in the Goma area, with no immediate plans for a complete evacuation.
"The situation is tense but not critical. We are watching developments closely," she added.
Aid officials in Goma, about 100 km (60 miles) north of Bukavu, said there were reports of small-arms fire at two refugee camps north of the town, but it was not clear what had happened.

The rebels have captured several towns and have panicked hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees into fleeing their camps, creating a major humanitarian problem in an area where aid facilities were already stretched.
